The **2006 FIFA World Cup final** was the final match of the [2006 World Cup](2006_FIFA_World_Cup "2006 FIFA World Cup"), the 18th edition of <FIFA>'s competition for national [football](Association_football "Association football") teams. The match was played at the [Olympiastadion](Olympiastadion_(Berlin) "Olympiastadion (Berlin)") in <Berlin>, Germany, on 9 July 2006, and was contested between [Italy](Italy_national_football_team "Italy national football team") and [France](France_national_football_team "France national football team"). The event comprised hosts [Germany](Germany_national_football_team "Germany national football team") and 31 other teams who emerged from [the qualification phase](2006_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification "2006 FIFA World Cup qualification"), organised by the six [FIFA confederations](List_of_football_federations#FIFA_Confederations "List of football federations"). The 32 teams competed in a group stage, from which 16 teams qualified for [the knockout stage](2006_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage "2006 FIFA World Cup knockout stage"). En route to the final, Italy finished first in [Group E](2014_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_E "2014 FIFA World Cup Group E"), with two wins and a draw, after which they defeated [Australia](Australia_national_football_team "Australia national football team") in the round of 16, [Ukraine](Ukraine_national_football_team "Ukraine national football team") in the quarter-final and Germany 2–0, in the semi-final. France finished runner-up of [Group G](2006_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_G "2006 FIFA World Cup Group G") with one win and two draws, before defeating [Spain](Spain_national_football_team "Spain national football team") in the round of 16, [Brazil](Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team") in the quarter-final and [Portugal](Portugal_national_football_team "Portugal national football team") 1–0 in the semi-final. The final was witnessed by 69,000 spectators in the stadium, with the referee for the match being [Horacio Elizondo](Horacio_Elizondo "Horacio Elizondo") from Argentina.

Italy won the World Cup after beating France 5–3 in a [penalty shoot-out](Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)") following a 1–1 draw at the conclusion of [extra time](Extra_time "Extra time"). The match was focused mostly on France's [Zinedine Zidane](Zinedine_Zidane "Zinedine Zidane") and Italy's [Marco Materazzi](Marco_Materazzi "Marco Materazzi"): this was the former's last match for France, they each scored their team's only goal of the game, and they were also involved in an incident in extra time that led to Zidane being sent off for headbutting Materazzi in the chest. The incident was the subject of much analysis following the match. Italy's [Andrea Pirlo](Andrea_Pirlo "Andrea Pirlo") was named the man of the match, and Zidane was awarded the [Golden Ball](FIFA_World_Cup_awards#Golden_Ball "FIFA World Cup awards") as the best player of the tournament.

The final served as a key match in the [France–Italy football rivalry](France%E2%80%93Italy_football_rivalry "France–Italy football rivalry"), coming after Italy were defeated by France in the [UEFA Euro 2000 final](UEFA_Euro_2000_final "UEFA Euro 2000 final"). Italy's victory was their first world title in 24 years, and their fourth overall, putting them one ahead of [Germany](Germany_national_football_team "Germany national football team") and only one behind [Brazil](Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team").
